authority: Explicit user instruction: include validation programs on both sides, or exclude them on both sides.

rules.validation: Apply the same inclusion rule to both sides. Optional validation excluded from both is the default.
rules.written_ratio: sum c(original manuscripts) / (c(whole topic common theory) + sum c(complete applications))
rules.conditional_ratio: c(original manuscript i) / c(complete application i), conditional on acquiring the whole common theory and every declared required dependency.
rules.validation_inclusive_ratio: (source written cost + source validation cost) / (replacement written cost + replacement validation cost), with matched scope and representation.
rules.required_computation: Algorithms, finite certificates and data used as proof premises retain their required status. A manuscript-length ratio is not a complete executable-proof cost ratio.
rules.unknown_costs: Uninventoried or inaccessible source software is unknown, not zero. Software-inclusive comparisons remain unavailable until both sides are inventoried under the same rule.
rules.embedded_listings: A claim that validation is excluded on both sides requires screening embedded listings too. Mathematical definitions, presentations and written algorithmic arguments are not optional validation listings.
rules.cross_topic_common_cost: Every topic pays its whole common theory independently. No overlap deduction across topics.
rules.manifest_history: Earlier frozen evidence remains intact. Its asymmetric software-inclusive fractions are withdrawn as compression measures, not silently recalculated.

current_measurement.written_scope: Complete manuscripts at the representations stated in written_topics.csv; separate programs excluded on both sides.
current_measurement.withdrawal_scope: All earlier factors formed by adding our programs or mandatory data only to the replacement denominator without corresponding source-side inventory. This includes optional-validation sensitivities.

new_expanded_F: Not admitted by this correction. The two-source scientific and numerical work remains in progress.
